title: BLOCKER: address_precision migrations must apply before the frontend that sends p_address_precision
body:
## Problem

`resolve_media_location` only gained `p_house_number` / `p_address_precision` in `supabase/migrations/20260910140000_upload_address_precision.sql:156`. The frontend on `cursor/upload-heic-hash-order-3be6` sends `p_address_precision` on **every** location write. If the app deploys before the migration applies, PostgREST cannot resolve the function for the parameter set it is given and every location write fails — for uploads that means addresses silently stop being persisted.

`supabase/migrations/20260910160000_fix_address_precision_overloads.sql` adds a second migration to the same chain, which widens the window rather than closing it.

## Evidence

- `apps/web/src/app/core/upload/address-resolution/upload-address-resolve.util.ts:66`, `:106`
- `apps/web/src/app/core/location-resolver/location-resolver.service.ts:439`, `:462`, `:522`
- `apps/web/src/app/core/media-location-update/media-location-update.service.ts:46`, `:99`, `:171`
- `apps/web/src/app/core/media-locations/adapters/supabase-media-locations.adapter.ts:134` (`patchToRpcParams`, shared by add/update/findOrCreate)

## Why it matters

Both halves are individually correct; nothing enforces the order between them. The failure is silent at the user level — the upload completes and the address never arrives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deploy order is written down where the deployer will see it (release notes or `supabase/AGENTS.md`)
- [ ] `supabase migration list` shows both migrations applied on hosted before the frontend build ships
- [ ] One upload with coordinates verified end-to-end after apply

**Source:** `docs/study/003-upload-precision-data-contract-review.md` finding 1 (lands with `cursor/upload-heic-hash-order-3be6`). Static review only — no database was reachable when this was written.

title: Verify the address_precision migrations against a real database (both are unverified)
body:
## Problem

`20260910140000_upload_address_precision.sql` and `20260910160000_fix_address_precision_overloads.sql` have never been applied in an agent environment — there are no Supabase credentials there. `20260910160000` was replayed locally against PostgreSQL 16; **hosted is unverified for both**. `20260910120000_retire_dedup_hashes_for_media_item.sql` is in the same state.

## Evidence

- `docs/specs/service/media-upload-service/address-resolution-model.address-precision-writers.supplement.md:5` records the unverified status
- `docs/specs/service/media-upload-service/address-resolution-model.md:46`

## Why it matters

The precision column is the foundation for map display, containment selection and dedupe keys. A migration that fails to apply, or applies with a different overload resolution than expected, breaks all of them at once — and the frontend already depends on it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both migrations applied to hosted; `supabase migration list` shows Local == Remote
- [ ] `resolve_media_location`, `add_media_item_location`, `list_locations_for_media` verified against `pg_proc` for the expected signatures
- [ ] One write/read round trip of `address_precision` confirmed

**Source:** `docs/study/003-upload-precision-data-contract-review.md` (§ measurement ceiling).

title: NF-39: reverse geocode runs unawaited, `resolving_address` is a false signal, geocoder failure is silent
body:
## Problem

Reverse geocoding runs inside `persistUploadFile` during the `saving_record` phase, **without `await`**. The post-save `resolving_address` phase awaits an empty stub. So the job reaches `complete` before the street address may exist, and on geocoder failure `location_status: 'unresolvable'` is written with no user-visible error.

## Evidence

- unawaited call: `apps/web/src/app/core/upload/support/upload-file-persist.util.ts:232-240`
- empty stub: `apps/web/src/app/core/upload/support/upload-enrichment.service.ts:43-47`
- cosmetic phase: `apps/web/src/app/core/upload/pipelines/new/upload-new-post-save.util.ts:146-147`
- silent failure: `apps/web/src/app/core/upload/address-resolution/upload-address-resolve.util.ts:22-24`, `:45-47`

## Why it matters

Violates the stated product principle in `upload-manager.md` ("uploading is a background task — don't make me think"): a user who cares about the address gets a green completion and no signal that it is missing. Supersedes UP-36.

## Product decision required (pick one or combine)

- **A** — await before `complete`
- **B** — async with a visible pending state
- **C** — retry on failure
- **D** — surface the failure (Issues lane or toast)

Minimum regardless of choice: stop emitting `resolving_address` around an empty method.

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 13](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md) · [`02-new-issues.md` NF-39](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/02-new-issues.md)

title: `count_zoomable_locations_for_media` and `locationPinEligible` use different rules, and nothing records it
body:
## Problem

The SQL counts links whose location has coordinates, with no street and no precision predicate. The client-side counterpart requires street text — and its comment claims the *"same rule as batch `zoomable_location_count`"*. The two rules are different.

## Evidence

- `supabase/migrations/20260524120000_locations_nn_junction.sql:467-482` (coords only)
- `apps/web/src/app/core/media-locations/media-locations.helpers.ts:309-325` (`countZoomableLinks` → `locationsWithGps` → `locationPinEligible`, street + coords)
- `rg 'count_zoomable_locations_for_media' docs/specs` returns **zero** hits

## Why it matters

Whoever implements the `locationPinEligible` removal will hit this divergence and have to re-derive it. A client and server disagreeing about "how many locations can be zoomed to" produces counts that do not match what the UI shows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The intended rule is stated once, in a spec
- [ ] Client and RPC agree, or the difference is documented with its reason

**Source:** `docs/study/003-upload-precision-data-contract-review.md` finding 5.

title: `retire_dedup_hashes_for_media_item` is org-scoped but not owner-scoped, and returns 0 silently for a missing media id
body:
## Problem

Two small holes in the same RPC (`supabase/migrations/20260910120000_retire_dedup_hashes_for_media_item.sql`):

1. It derives the organization server-side and raises `42501` across organizations (`:28-31`) — the tenant boundary holds — but it does **not** check who uploaded the media item. Any authenticated member can retire any other member's dedup hashes for any media id in the org, re-opening the duplicate-upload window the hashes exist to close.
2. It returns `0` for a media id that does not exist (`:24-26`), which is indistinguishable from "nothing to retire". A replace flow passing a stale id gets a success-shaped answer.

## Why it matters

Low blast radius (bounded by tenant, damage is duplicate rows rather than data loss) but it is a wider grant than the replace flow needs, and the silent zero hides a caller bug.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide whether owner scoping is required; implement or document the decision
- [ ] Missing media id is distinguishable from "zero retired"

**Source:** `docs/study/003-upload-precision-data-contract-review.md` findings 7–8. Static review — the RPC was never executed.

title: UP-05: `beforeunload` handler is an empty function — closing the tab mid-upload warns nobody
body:
## Problem

`private readonly beforeUnloadHandler = (): void => {};` — the handler is registered but does nothing, so closing or reloading the tab during an active upload produces no browser warning.

## Evidence

- `apps/web/src/app/core/upload/upload-manager.service.ts:239` (definition), `:262` (registration)

## Why it matters

An in-flight upload that is killed by a tab close leaves storage/row residue and loses the user's work with no prompt. The acceptance criterion for this is correctly left unticked in the spec, so the gap is known and unfixed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Handler calls `preventDefault()` / sets `returnValue` only while upload work is active
- [ ] Any copy involved goes through the i18n pipeline

**Source:** [`04-status-of-prior-findings.md` § 3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/04-status-of-prior-findings.md) · improvement plan item 10.

title: UP-14: `revokeLocalUrl` is defined and never called — object URLs leak for the panel's lifetime
body:
## Problem

`MediaDownloadService.revokeLocalUrl` exists and delegates to the signed-URL cache, but nothing in the upload lifecycle ever calls it. Object URLs created for previews are never revoked.

## Evidence

- `apps/web/src/app/core/media-download/media-download.service.ts:382-383`
- `apps/web/src/app/core/media-download/adapters/signed-url-cache.adapter.ts:171`
- No call sites outside those definitions

## Why it matters

A long upload session with many previews holds every blob in memory until the page is reloaded. Cheap to fix, invisible until it is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Called on job remove, complete, and cancel
- [ ] A test pins the call for at least one of those paths

**Source:** [`04-status-of-prior-findings.md` § 3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/04-status-of-prior-findings.md) · improvement plan item 10.

title: UP-25: two incompatible `ImageUploadedEvent` types, disambiguated by an alias
body:
## Problem

The same event name is declared twice with different shapes — once in the upload module and once in the workspace-pane module — and the lifecycle service reconciles them with an import alias.

## Evidence

- `apps/web/src/app/core/upload/upload-manager.types.ts` (upload-side shape)
- `apps/web/src/app/core/workspace-pane/workspace-pane-shell-events.types.ts:7`
- Consumers: `core/route-session-cache/route-session-cache.service.ts:4`, `features/map/map-shell/handlers/map-placement.service.ts:15`

## Why it matters

Two types with one name is a trap for anyone adding a field: the compiler accepts the change on one side and the runtime payload disagrees.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One canonical type; the other is an alias or is deleted
- [ ] No import aliasing remains to hide the collision

**Source:** [`04-status-of-prior-findings.md` § 3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/04-status-of-prior-findings.md) · improvement plan item 10.

title: UP-26: 20 circular imports across core/upload, worked around with `injector.get`
body:
## Problem

`madge --circular src/app/core/upload` reports **20** cycles (the earlier audit recorded 11), all threading `UploadLocationResolutionService` ↔ `UploadManagerService` ↔ the pipelines. The workaround in place is deferred resolution via `injector.get`.

## Evidence

- `apps/web/src/app/core/upload/location/upload-location-disambiguation-registration.service.ts:27`, `:126`, `:128`
- Reproduce: `npx madge --circular apps/web/src/app/core/upload`

## Why it matters

Cycles make the pipeline consolidation work (improvement plan item 4) more expensive and hide initialization-order bugs behind lazy lookups.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Narrow event/port interfaces replace the back-references
- [ ] `madge --circular` reports 0 for `core/upload`
- [ ] No `injector.get` workarounds remain for this reason

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 8](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md)

title: UP-34: "re-queues the job at the front of the queue" is documented but not implemented
body:
## Problem

`UploadManagerService.resolveConflict`'s doc comment states it "re-queues the job at the front of the concurrency queue". The queue selector is plain array order with filters — there is no front-of-queue behaviour anywhere.

## Evidence

- claim: `apps/web/src/app/core/upload/upload-manager.service.ts:418-422`
- implementation: `apps/web/src/app/core/upload/manager/upload-manager-queue.util.ts:14-20`

## Why it matters

A user who just answered a tray question waits behind everything queued before them, and the code says otherwise. Either behaviour is defensible; the mismatch is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement priority ordering for user-resolved jobs, **or** delete the claim from the comment and any spec that repeats it

**Source:** [`04-status-of-prior-findings.md` § 3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/04-status-of-prior-findings.md)

title: UP-38: `media-item-upload-overlay.md` is 253 lines — 73 over the 180-line spec cap
body:
## Problem

The three specs named in the earlier audit were split; this one was not. `wc -l docs/specs/component/media/media-item-upload-overlay.md` → **253**, against an error cap of 180.

## Why it matters

It is one of the 198 errors currently reported by `node scripts/verify.mjs specs`, and the ratchet in `AGENTS.md` says that count may only go down.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Split into linked children (`*.supplement.md` / `*.acceptance-criteria.md`) per the split policy in `AGENTS.md`
- [ ] `node scripts/verify.mjs specs` error count drops by one

**Source:** [`04-status-of-prior-findings.md` § 4](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/04-status-of-prior-findings.md)

title: Consolidate the three upload pipelines around a shared prepare and commit tail
body:
## Problem

New, attach and replace each re-implement validate → EXIF → convert → dedup → upload → post-write. Every hardening fix in the NF-01…NF-10 pass had to land three times, and two of them reached only one pipeline before the integration pass caught it.

## Proposed shape

| Layer | Shared module | Pipelines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prepare | `upload-pipeline-prepare.util.ts` | validate, EXIF, HEIC, dedup |
| Storage write | `runStorageUploadWithTimeout` + `persistUploadFile` | all three |
| Post-write | `upload-db-postwrite.util.ts`, cancel residue | all three |
| Mode tail | thin adapters | new / attach / replace |

**Must stay separate:** new (pre-resolve location, conflict check), attach (link existing row, `verifyStoragePathWrite`, no row delete on cancel), replace (`oldStoragePath` restore, `retireStaleDedupHashes`, update not insert).

## Why it matters

This is the structural cause of the "fixed once, still broken twice" pattern that produced NF-05, NF-06 and NF-10.

**Change class:** Sensitive. ~15–20 files, mostly extraction.

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 4](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md)

title: Upload commit point: make cleanup state-driven instead of call-site-driven
body:
## Problem

The storage write and the `media_items` insert are two systems with no transaction between them. Cleanup for each failure window is handled per call site, so every new path has to remember to do it — and the sign-out path already proved that it will not.

## Evidence

- storage write `apps/web/src/app/core/upload/support/upload-file-persist.util.ts:92-101`
- row insert `:190-213`, rollback on DB failure `:215-219`

## Proposed change (incremental)

- Track `persistStage: 'none' | 'storage_written' | 'row_committed'` on the job
- One `abortJobPersist(job)` that cleans up from the stage it is in
- Replace path takes the **restore** branch, not delete-row
- Sign-out guard calls the same entry point

Start with the stage enum and a single abort function; do not build an abstract coordinator first.

**Change class:** Sensitive (data integrity).

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 5](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md)

title: G5: a second folder drop re-asks a tray question that is already pending for the first
body:
## Problem

Disambiguation groups are scoped per `batchId`. When a user adds a second folder with overlapping addresses while the first is still unresolved, the second batch finds no resolved location, runs its own Photon call, and opens its own tray for the same physical address — sometimes with different candidate text.

## Proposed change

Session-scoped index keyed by `(field, conflicting-value-set)`: reuse a resolved answer, merge `jobIds` into an open tray, skip the duplicate geocode call.

## Why it matters

The highest-frequency remaining tray annoyance: the user answers the same question twice for the same building. The required behaviour is already written in `address-resolution-model.md` § Cross-batch same-address dedup with an unchecked acceptance criterion.

**Change class:** Sensitive (address-resolution orchestrator). No DB migration.

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 6](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md) · [`03-hard-cases-and-decisions.md` § F3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/03-hard-cases-and-decisions.md)

title: Integration specs for the upload failure windows that no test currently covers
body:
## Problem

Cancel timing, sign-out mid-flight, and replace-cancel-after-row-update are the three most damaging upload paths and none is exercised in CI. They are exactly the paths where the last audit found live defects (NF-02, NF-03).

## Proposed change

Extend the `upload-folder-upload.integration.spec.ts` pattern with:

- cancel mid-upload (between storage write and row insert)
- sign-out before and after the storage write
- replace cancel after the row update — assert `storage_path` is restored, not left dangling

## Why it matters

Without these, the commit-coordinator work and the pipeline consolidation have no safety net, and both are Sensitive-class changes that require red-test-first.

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 7](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md)

title: Commit a real device-exported HEIC fixture (the repo has none)
body:
## Problem

There are zero `.heic` / `.heif` files in the repository; `apps/web/public/vienna_sample_photos/` is JPEG-only. The NF-38 encoder-determinism experiment had to use synthetic HEIC containers generated with `pillow-heif` — valid HEVC HEIF, but not iPhone exports.

## Why it matters

HEIC is the primary input format from construction-site iPhones. Live Photo bursts, HDR and depth maps were not covered by the experiment, and the dedup fingerprint path is the thing they would break.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least one real device-exported HEIC committed as a fixture
- [ ] Conversion + `photo_v1` fingerprint asserted on it in CI

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 7](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md) · [`02-new-issues.md` § 3 NF-38](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/02-new-issues.md)

title: Write the LIVE VERIFICATION block for replace-cancel and sign-out residue
body:
## Problem

Both paths are Sensitive-class and neither can be proven in CI without a browser and a live backend. `AGENTS.md` requires a LIVE VERIFICATION block for exactly this situation, and none exists for them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A named, step-by-step browser check for: cancel a replace after the row update, then inspect `storage_path`
- [ ] A named check for: start an upload, sign out mid-flight, then list the bucket prefix and query the row as admin
- [ ] Both linked from the upload specs so a reviewer can find them

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 7](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md) · `docs/agent-workflows/agent-communication.md` § LIVE VERIFICATION

title: Unbuilt upload features still carry active acceptance criteria — build, defer, or remove
body:
## Problem

Four features are described in specs with unchecked acceptance criteria and no implementation. Per the Change-Completeness Rule in `AGENTS.md`, unchecked AC for unbuilt behaviour is a trust problem: the next reader cannot tell what ships.

| Feature | User impact | Recommendation from the audit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **G4** deferred-address lifecycle | Medium — Skip writes `failed` + `pendingPartialLocation`, not a durable `deferred` | Build if the product wants "answer later", or remove the AC |
| **G1** sibling-folder conflict | Low frequency | Remove from active AC unless the product confirms |
| **C5** `context_distance` tray | None — the filter ships, the tray never fires | Already demoted to the deferred backlog; confirm the union member is gone |
| **Step 4** `exifContextCheck` | None — config flag with **zero** runtime consumers (`apps/web/src/app/core/upload/location/upload-location-config.ts:27`, `:71`) | Build the check or remove it from the active AC |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the four is either built, or its AC is moved to a clearly-marked deferred section
- [ ] `exifContextCheck` is either consumed or deleted

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 11](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md). Related: existing issue #22 (verify remaining media upload acceptance criteria).

title: Capture the geocoder bounding box — it arrives on every response and is thrown away
body:
## Problem

Nominatim returns `boundingbox` on the responses the `/geocode` edge function already proxies verbatim (`supabase/functions/geocode/index.ts:366-371`). The client never reads it: `boundingbox` has **zero** occurrences in `apps/web/src/app/core/geocoding/`. There is no extent stored on `locations`.

## Why it matters

Every precision-aware map behaviour depends on knowing how large a coarse location is — containment selection, area rendering, and the disclosure line after a circle selection. Capturing it costs **no extra requests**; the data is already on the wire.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Geocode parse types carry the bounding box on forward and reverse paths
- [ ] Extent persisted on `locations` (bbox columns or a PostGIS envelope) — migration required
- [ ] Existing rows without an extent behave as before

**Source:** [`address-resolution-model.area-extent-decisions.supplement.md` § Decision 3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/specs/service/media-upload-service/address-resolution-model.area-extent-decisions.supplement.md) · [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 15](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md)

title: Radius selection uses centroid distance, not containment of the known area
body:
## Problem

`RadiusSelectionService.selectRadiusImages` tests `map.distance(center, cell) <= radiusMeters` against marker coordinates — centroid distance, with no extent and no precision gate. A city-precision photo sitting at a centroid is selected when the user circles a single block.

## Evidence

- `apps/web/src/app/features/map/map-shell/radius/radius-selection.service.ts:56-60`
- Decision (2026-09-10): [`address-resolution-model.area-extent-decisions.supplement.md` § Decision 1](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/specs/service/media-upload-service/address-resolution-model.area-extent-decisions.supplement.md)

## Why it matters

Selection drives project creation and workspace curation. Including a photo whose real location is "somewhere in Vienna" in a block-sized selection is a silent correctness bug in the user's data, not a cosmetic one.

## Depends on

Stored extent (bbox capture issue) and the geometry decision — see the product-decision issue for `STUDY-001`, which proposes an equal-area disc instead of bbox-corner containment.

**Change class:** Sensitive. Red-test-first: a `Vienna/` fixture excluded from a block-sized radius, included when the circle covers the whole area.

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 15](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md)

title: Remove `locationPinEligible` and drive map affordances from `address_precision` — but only with a replacement
body:
## Problem

`locationPinEligible(row)` returns true only when `row.street` is non-empty and the coordinates are valid (`apps/web/src/app/core/media-locations/media-locations.helpers.ts:309-315`). It keys on **address text** to decide whether to trust a **coordinate** — a proxy condition for precision, which is now stored explicitly. Product decision 2 (2026-09-10) retires it.

## The trap

It does **not** gate the map's marker query: `viewport_markers` selects every link with coordinates and `geog` (`supabase/migrations/20260524120000_locations_nn_junction.sql:757`). So city-precision rows already render as ordinary point pins today. Deleting the gate without a coarse-area representation makes the map **more** misleading, not less — the pin stays and the one signal saying "do not zoom to this point" is gone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Precision-driven rendering ships **with or before** the removal, never after
- [ ] No remaining references to `locationPinEligible` in `apps/web/src` or `docs/specs`
- [ ] Visual treatment approved separately (see the coarse-precision map UX decision issue) — this issue is behaviour only

**Source:** [`address-resolution-model.area-extent-decisions.supplement.md` § Decision 2](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/specs/service/media-upload-service/address-resolution-model.area-extent-decisions.supplement.md) · `docs/study/002-coarse-precision-map-ux.md` § 2

title: Align `viewport_markers` with the precision-aware zoomable rule
body:
## Problem

The spec said address-only rows are excluded from `viewport_markers`; the SQL filters on coordinates and `geog` only. The RPC and its contract have drifted.

## Evidence

- `supabase/migrations/20260524120000_locations_nn_junction.sql:757` and its `WHERE` clause (org + coords + `geog` + viewport intersect)
- `docs/specs/service/media-locations/media-locations.zoomable-map-contract.supplement.md` § 10

## Also worth recording

Neither `viewport_markers` nor `cluster_images` (`supabase/migrations/20260525130000_drop_media_items_location_columns.sql:248`) carries a `media_type` predicate. **The map shows all media with coordinates, not photos only** — any copy or estimate written as "photos" is wrong for mixed batches.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] RPC filter (or a documented client post-filter) matches the zoomable contract
- [ ] The `media_type` scope is stated in the contract

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 15](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md) · `docs/study/001-area-selection-geometry.md` § 7

title: Phase collapse (20 → 13–15) is now unblocked — decide whether to do it
body:
## Context

Collapsing `UploadPhase` was rejected in 2026-09-09 (H3) because all 20 members are reachable and no transition map existed, making a collapse a behaviour change with no guard. **The transition map has since landed** on `cursor/upload-heic-hash-order-3be6`, so the stated blocker is gone.

## The question

Is the phase noise worth a Sensitive-class change now, or is 20 phases acceptable given each maps to a distinct user-facing status label?

## If it goes ahead

- [ ] Tests per merged phase before merging any
- [ ] Subscribers and status labels re-checked (`queued` has 12 writers, `complete` has 8)

**Source:** [`06-improvement-plan.md` item 12](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/06-improvement-plan.md) · [`03-hard-cases-and-decisions.md` § H3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/03-hard-cases-and-decisions.md)

title: Product decision: area-selection geometry for coarse locations (equal-area disc vs bbox corners)
body:
## Decision needed

Product decision 1 (2026-09-10) defines containment as **every corner of the location's bounding box inside the circle**. `STUDY-001` argues that produces a corner artifact large enough to be user-visible, and proposes an equal-area disc instead.

## The numbers (measured via a one-off Nominatim lookup — graded `[B]`, not Feldpost's own geocoder)

- Vienna's bbox: 29.4 km × 22.8 km ≈ **669 km²** — about **61 % larger** than Vienna's ~415 km² administrative area
- Containing all four corners needs a selection radius of ≈ **19.7 km**
- Equal-area disc `r = sqrt(w·h/π)` gives ≈ **14.6 km**
- Disc containment using the circumscribed (half-diagonal) radius is equivalent to the corner test — it removes the corner comparisons but not the corner geometry, so it buys nothing

## The honest cost of the proposal

The equal-area disc under-covers the bbox corners by up to ~5 km for Vienna, so for radii between ~14.6 km and ~19.8 km it includes items a strict whole-bbox rule would exclude.

## Also settled in the study

Tier-identity inclusion ("include everything whose city matches an area in play") is not viable as the primary rule: a circle holding only coarse markers selects nothing, and one precise pin in one district would pull in every `city=Wien` item org-wide.

**Source:** `docs/study/001-area-selection-geometry.md` (status `proposed` — **not accepted**; lands with `cursor/upload-heic-hash-order-3be6`).

title: Product decisions pending: how coarse-precision media appears on the map
body:
## Decisions needed

From `docs/study/002-coarse-precision-map-ux.md` (status `proposed`). All four are product calls, not engineering ones.

1. **Area-marker visual treatment.** Coarse media must stay visible but must never render as a point pin on a centroid. What it looks like instead is **gated on explicit sign-off** per the component styling gate in `AGENTS.md` — no SCSS or marker code may be touched before then.
2. **Disclosure copy after a circle selection.** The study proposes one quiet line — *"N more in Wien", tap to include* — rather than silence or a precision-jargon banner. Multi-city overlap copy is undecided: one line per city, or one aggregate line?
3. **Rectangle honesty.** The stored extent is an axis-aligned box ~61 % larger than Vienna's real area. Should the UI ever say so, or is the approximation silent?
4. **Should committing a search populate the workspace selection?**

## Already answered by the study (no decision needed)

- Retrieval for coarse media is **non-spatial and already shipped**: `app-filter-dropdown` and `app-grouping-dropdown` on `/media` (`apps/web/src/app/features/media/media.component.html:106`, `:115`) with `address` and `city` as built-in metadata fields (`apps/web/src/app/core/metadata/adapters/built-in-metadata-fields.adapter.ts:17-18`). **No new component is needed.**
- **No post-upload refinement prompts** — that would violate "uploading is a background task, don't make me think". Media Detail editing and Uploaded-lane row actions already cover refinement, unprompted.

**Caveat carried by the study:** every user-behaviour claim in it is an inference with no user research behind it.

title: Cluster click and radius selection use different geometries — should they agree?
body:
## Problem

Three different geometries are in play for "what did I just select":

- **Radius selection** — centroid distance today, containment by decision (`apps/web/src/app/features/map/map-shell/radius/radius-selection.service.ts:56-60`)
- **Cluster click** — grid-snapped centroid cells (`supabase/migrations/20260525130000_drop_media_items_location_columns.sql:248`, `cluster_images`)
- **Proposed** — equal-area disc containment for coarse tiers

## The question

Should clicking a cluster follow the same containment rule as drawing a circle? Today they diverge, so the same set of photos can be in one selection and out of the other.

This is a product call about selection semantics, not a refactor.

**Source:** `docs/study/002-coarse-precision-map-ux.md` § open questions.

title: Spec lint debt: 198 errors reported by `npm run verify` (soft check, ratchet)
body:
## Problem

`node scripts/verify.mjs specs` reports **198 errors and 37 warnings across 183 specs** (measured 2026-09-10; was 201 on 2026-09-08). Mostly `spec-max-lines` and missing required sections. The check is wired into `verify` as **soft** — it reports and does not fail — because it was already red before the gate existed.

## Why it matters

`AGENTS.md` declares the count a ratchet that may only go down. A soft check that stays red for months is a check people learn to ignore, which is how it got to 198 in the first place.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide **per rule**, not per file: fix the class (most are size caps with a documented split remedy) or move genuinely-exempt paths into `shouldIncludeSpecFile()` with the reason in the commit
- [ ] Burn-down tracked in `docs/specs/SPEC-SIZE-BACKLOG.md`
- [ ] Promote `specs` from soft to hard once it reaches 0

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` A5](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) · `AGENTS.md` § `npm run verify`

title: ESLint debt: 151 errors + 1068 warnings, and `--max-warnings 0` means warnings fail too
body:
## Problem

The `lint` step of `npm run verify` was measured at **151 errors and 1068 warnings** on `main` (2026-09-08) and entered the gate as a **soft** check for that reason. With `--max-warnings 0`, every warning is a failure once the check is promoted.

## Why it matters

The declared ratchet in `AGENTS.md` says the number may only go down — but nobody is burning it down, and a permanently-soft lint check trains people to ignore lint output entirely.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Re-measure on `main` and record the current number
- [ ] Group the errors by rule and fix or explicitly disable per rule, with the reason
- [ ] Promote `lint` from soft to hard when it reaches 0

**Source:** `AGENTS.md` § `npm run verify` · [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` A5](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md)

title: Re-baseline the `test` ratchet in AGENTS.md — the bundle compiles again, and 39 tests fail at runtime
body:
## Problem

`AGENTS.md` § `npm run verify` still describes the `test` check as "**the test bundle does not compile** — ~101 TS errors, 4 unresolved imports in `*.spec.ts`", measured 2026-09-08. **That is stale.** Measured 2026-09-10 with `npx ng test --watch=false`:

```
Test Files  15 failed | 177 passed (192)
     Tests  39 failed | 1229 passed | 5 expected fail (1273)
    Errors  34 errors
```

Zero TypeScript compile errors; 192 files and 1273 tests execute. Compile debt is cleared and **execution** debt replaced it. The 39 failures sit in 15 files, none in the upload subsystem, and are runtime mock drift — the largest cluster is `workspace-view.grouping.spec.ts` calling `.order()` on a Supabase mock chain that does not provide it, which also produces most of the 34 unhandled rejections.

## Why it matters

A ratchet that says "does not compile" invites the next agent to assume tests are unrunnable and skip them. The number should be re-measured on `main`, not on a branch — re-baselining governance is the owner's call.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` ratchet re-measured on `main` and rewritten
- [ ] The Supabase mock chain in `workspace-view.grouping.spec.ts` provides `.order()`
- [ ] Failure count recorded as the new ratchet

**Source:** [`04-status-of-prior-findings.md` § 1](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/upload-flow-review-2026-09-10/04-status-of-prior-findings.md)

title: Label taxonomy: two parallel priority schemes are live (`P1`/`P2`/`P3` and `priority:P1`…)
body:
## Problem

The repository carries **both** priority label families at once:

- bare `P1`, `P2`, `P3` (grey, no description) — used by issues #59–#89
- `priority:P0`…`priority:P3` (described: P0 security/data loss/release-blocking, P1 user-blocking, P2 confirmed bounded bug or spec drift, P3 hypothesis/cleanup/product decision) — used by issues #9–#57 and everything filed since

So "all P2 issues" is two different queries and neither is complete.

## Why it matters

The register is only useful if a filter returns the whole set. Two schemes means triage silently misses half the backlog.

## Proposed resolution

Keep `priority:PN` — it is the described scheme, it has a P0 tier, and it is what recent issues use. Migrate the bare labels onto it, then delete them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every issue carrying a bare `P1`/`P2`/`P3` also carries the `priority:PN` equivalent
- [ ] Bare `P1`/`P2`/`P3` labels deleted
- [ ] The scheme is named in `CONTRIBUTING.md` so the next person does not invent a third

**Note:** filed rather than executed — renaming labels touches every open issue and is the owner's call.

title: B2: assert that every `var(--x)` in the app resolves to a defined custom property
body:
## Problem

A `var(--transition-geometry)` that does not exist does not error — the declaration is dropped and the property never applies. The symptom is "the animation does nothing", which reliably sends people off refactoring logic instead of checking the token name.

`docs/design/agent-css-variable-contract.md` already says **"no invented variable names"** and lists forbidden legacy names. Nothing checks, and the legacy denylist only knows the four prefixes someone remembered to add.

## Proposed change (~30 lines)

Collect defined custom properties from `apps/web/src/styles.scss` and `styles/**`, scan every `.scss` / `.ts` / `.html` for `var(--…)`, fail on any name that is not defined. Handle third-party and runtime-injected names with an explicit allowlist constant, not by loosening the regex.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` B2](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P0 in the priority table.

title: E3: one skills source — 11 skills exist twice and two have already drifted
body:
## Problem

Every skill exists as both `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and `.cursor/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Nine pairs are byte-identical; **two have drifted**: `.cursor/skills/component-structure` carries an *FSM ↔ CSS ↔ DOM* section and `.cursor/skills/implement-from-spec` carries *Stateful / layered UI (FSM) — extra gates*, neither of which exists in the `.github/` copy.

## Why it matters

A Copilot session is running an older contract than a Cursor session and nothing reports it. Same failure mode as maintaining two instruction files.

## Proposed change

1. Re-apply the two drifted sections to the survivor **first**, so nothing is lost
2. Pick one canonical location; make the others pointers
3. Add a gate: fail if two files with the same skill name differ
4. Same treatment for `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, which restates ~50 lines of `AGENTS.md`

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` E3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P0.

title: D1: create `docs/TRAPS.md` — the expensive lessons live only in dated diary entries
body:
## Problem

Feldpost's most costly lessons exist as narrative inside dated diary files and one Cursor rule. An agent resuming work reads *the latest* diary entry for its area — it will not find a trap recorded eight weeks earlier under a different area.

## Seed entries (harvest these five)

- the stale unlayered-CSS escape hatch (`docs/ai-diary/2026-07-01.md`, second recurrence)
- cross-file injector pollution in the upload spec (`2026-05-27`)
- the warm-revisit media-grid regression (`docs/migration/reports/…-2026-05-27`)
- the dead `project_address_a/b` fields (`2026-06-13`)
- the photon curl gate (`2026-05-25`)

## Format

Newest at top, three lines per entry: **what looked right · what was actually true · the check that would have caught it**. Entries are never deleted, only marked resolved. Link from `AGENTS.md` as *"read this before your second attempt"* — that is the moment it pays for itself.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` D1](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P0.

title: F2: add the two-attempt rule and revert-before-retry to the anti-patterns
body:
## Problem

`docs/agent-workflows/agent-communication.md` § Anti-patterns has no stopping rule. `docs/ai-diary/2026-07-01.md` records a bug caused by an escape hatch added during an *earlier* attempt at a different problem: **a fix that did not work is not neutral, it is now a confounding variable.**

## Proposed change (two paragraphs)

1. Revert the failed attempt before trying the next idea.
2. After two failures, stop. Summarise what was tried and what the user is actually seeing, then offer **two** options with a recommendation.

Plus: *when the user says "it works if I turn this off", that is the answer* — treat it as the lead, not as one data point among many.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` F2](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P0.

title: B1: turn the token gate from a value denylist into pattern rules
body:
## Problem

`scripts/lint-design-tokens.mjs` forbids **five specific hex strings**, four `var(--…)` prefixes and one file's z-index. A brand-new `#3a7bd5` in a component passes.

## Measured debt

| Pattern | Count |
| --- | --- |
| raw numeric `z-index:` | 77 |
| raw `…ms` durations | 165 |
| `cubic-bezier(` | 11 |
| raw hex outside `styles.scss` | **0** |

## Proposed change

Adopt a `RULES` array: `hex-color`, `color-function`, `arbitrary-z-index`, `off-scale-duration`, `raw-easing`, each with a message naming the fix. Scope `apps/web/src/app/**`, excluding `styles.scss` and `styles/**` (they *are* the token source). Add a `token-check-ignore` escape hatch requiring a reason on the same line.

**Land colors as errors immediately — the migration cost is zero today.** Land z-index / duration / easing as warnings with a burn-down, promote when they hit 0.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` B1](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: B3: put the contrast audit into `design-system:check` instead of next to it
body:
## Problem

`scripts/audit-theme-contrast.mjs` exists but is wired only to `design-system:contrast-audit`. It is **not** in `design-system:check`, so it never runs in CI.

## Why it matters

Feldpost has two themes plus a sandstone variant. A palette tuned by eye in light mode with a dark variant that quietly drops below 4.5:1 is exactly what a gate is for.

## Proposed change

Add it to `design-system:check` (and therefore to `verify`). Adopt an explicit `PAIRS` list — `[foreground, background, minRatio, what it is used for]` — evaluated in **both** themes, and **fail when a token has no pair**, so a new token is untested loudly rather than silently.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` B3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: C2: add `npm run new:spec` and `npm run new:use-case` scaffolders
body:
## Problem

The spec format lives in `docs/agent-workflows/element-spec-format.md` — a document an agent must find, read and obey. Nothing makes the correct shape the default output.

## Proposed change

Scaffolders that emit the skeleton with required sections in canonical order, the next free `UC-NNN`, the id comments, and the index row.

## Why it matters

This is what makes the traceability and `## Check` gates cheap instead of a tax — build it before enforcing those.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` C2](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: E2: replace `docs/SESSION_START.md` with a real SessionStart hook
body:
## Problem

`docs/SESSION_START.md` is a prompt a human is asked to copy-paste into Cursor at the start of every session. Anything depending on a human remembering to paste a prompt fails at exactly the moment it matters — a fresh cloud session with no `node_modules`, where the first `npm test` fails for a reason unrelated to the code.

## Proposed change

`.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`: install dependencies if missing, print three orientation lines (branch, last 5 commits, where the specs index is). Keep `SESSION_START.md` as the documented equivalent for tools without hooks, but make the hook the primary path.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` E2](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: E4: ship the reviewer subagent the Sensitive change class requires
body:
## Problem

`AGENTS.md` requires "fresh-context adversarial review by a different agent than the implementer" for Sensitive changes. `.github/agents/revy-the-reviewer.agent.md` exists for Copilot; Claude Code has no equivalent — so in practice the requirement is met by the implementer re-reading their own diff, which is the one thing it forbids: **the implementer cannot see the assumption they made.**

## Proposed change

`.claude/agents/reviewer.md` with a restricted tool set (`Read, Grep, Glob, Bash`) and a priority order: unmet acceptance criteria → leftovers (grep the removed symbol across `apps/web/src` **and** `docs/specs/`) → state coherence → terminal states → tests that cannot fail → `AGENTS.md` boundaries. Explicitly **not** style.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` E4](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: F1: promote the idea-to-ship pipeline into the Required Feature Workflow
body:
## Problem

`docs/playbooks/idea-to-ship-pipeline.md` carries the 8 stages, the Definition of Ready, the Definition of Done, EARS/Given-When-Then, and the state-coherence contract. `AGENTS.md` mentions it twice, both times *inside* a sentence about something else. The **Required Feature Workflow** section — the one agents actually follow — does not link it, so the DoR/DoD gates are effectively optional.

## Proposed change

- Add it to the top of the document-authority list as *the* workflow document
- Make stage 1 (Definition of Ready) an explicit precondition in the change-class table

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` F1](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: D2: create `docs/adr/` with a template and sequential numbering
body:
## Problem

Hard, expensive-to-reverse decisions are recorded in whatever file was open at the time: `docs/design/design-system/registry-format-decision.md`, `docs/migration/decisions-log.md`, `docs/migration/reports/agent-token-decision-closure.md`. None is findable from a decision-shaped question, and none records the **rejected alternative** — the part that stops a decision being quietly reversed.

## Proposed change

`0000-template.md` + `README.md` index. Write ADRs going forward; retro-fit only the four or five that keep getting re-litigated: spec folder taxonomy · registry format · RLS as *the* boundary · Tailwind + SCSS coexistence · `docs/specs/` over `docs/element-specs/`. Never edit history — a superseded ADR stays, marked superseded.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` D2](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: D3: write a product-level `docs/CONSTITUTION.md`
body:
## Problem

`docs/design/constitution.md` covers *design* non-negotiables. There is no equivalent for correctness, data and failure — and Feldpost handles personal data under DSGVO with RLS as its only real boundary.

The rules that must outrank a direct instruction are currently implicit: *delete means delete* · *no silent failure* · *an empty `catch` is a bug* · *accessibility is not waivable for a deadline* · *nothing ships that nobody can explain*.

## Proposed change

One page, seven clauses, explicitly ranked above every other document. `design/constitution.md` becomes its design chapter. Amendment = a PR that changes only that file.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` D3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: C3: cap `AGENTS.md` at 150 lines and enforce it
body:
## Problem

`AGENTS.md` is **292 lines** and has absorbed a phase-specific migration exemption, a dead-code inventory naming three components, and a parallel-streams coordination note. Anything longer than about 150 lines gets skimmed instead of read — and skimming an instruction file is worse than a short one, because the reader believes they read it.

## Proposed change

Move out, leaving a one-line pointer for each:

- migration exemption → `docs/migration/README.md`
- archive inventory → `apps/web/src/app/archive/README.md`
- parallel-streams note → the migration index (which already claims to be the single queue)
- spec-split policy body → `docs/specs/README.md`

Then add the line-cap assertion to `scripts/lint-specs.mjs`.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` C3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: D6: write down the diary's rules (append-only, promote-or-lose)
body:
## Problem

`docs/ai-diary/README.md` explains what the diary *is* but not how to keep it honest.

## Proposed change (about eight lines)

- **Append, never rewrite** — a past entry that turned out wrong stays; the correction goes in a later entry
- **Entries are never deleted**
- **Skip the day if nothing was learned** — a diary of empty entries teaches people to stop opening it
- **Promotion rule** — a lesson is *noticed* in the diary and *promoted* to a trap, a pitfall, or a spec. A rule that lives only in a diary entry will be missed.

Plus a filename assertion (`YYYY-MM-DD.md`) in `scripts/lint-specs.mjs` so "the latest entry" is a question with an answer.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` D6](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: B5: two-way traceability between specs and use cases
body:
## Problem

21 use-case documents, 307 specs. **18 specs** reference a use case; **0 use cases** carry an ID. There is no way to answer "if this requirement changes, what breaks?" — and three use-case files still link `../archive/use-cases-README.md`, which no longer exists.

## Proposed change

`<!-- id: UC-NNN -->` / `<!-- specs: … -->` in the use case, `<!-- use-case: UC-NNN -->` in the spec, and `scripts/lint-specs.mjs` fails when either side does not resolve.

**Stage it:** new and edited specs must carry the link; backfill per area when that area is touched. Do not attempt 307 at once.

**Depends on** the use-case ID scheme (`UC-NNN` issue) and is much cheaper after the scaffolders exist.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` B5](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: B6: every spec names one runnable check
body:
## Problem

`REQUIRED_SECTIONS` in `scripts/lint-specs.mjs` already demands *Acceptance Criteria* — but nothing demands a way to run them. **0 of 307** specs have a `## Check` section; 36 mention any command at all. "It builds" is the de facto acceptance for most contracts.

## Proposed change

Add `## Check` to `docs/agent-workflows/element-spec-format.md` and to `CANONICAL_ORDER`. The line names one command (`ng test --include=…`, `npm run design-system:check`, or a `*.spec.ts` path) and the linter asserts the referenced test file exists.

Enforce for new and edited specs first (a `git diff`-scoped mode), then per area.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` B6](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P1.

title: A4: pin the Node version — `.nvmrc` and `engines`
body:
## Problem

Neither `.nvmrc` nor an `engines` field exists at the repository root. CI picks a version, contributors pick another, and `ng build` fails differently in each.

## Proposed change

`.nvmrc` plus `"engines": { "node": ">=22" }` in the root `package.json`, matching what CI uses.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` A4](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P2.

title: B7: ban raw color values inside spec markdown
body:
## Problem

`docs/specs/README.md` already says *"Specs describe token names … not hex literals"*. Nothing enforces it.

## Proposed change

One rule in `scripts/lint-specs.mjs`: hex / `rgb(` / `oklch(` in a spec body → error, with the message "values live in `apps/web/src/styles.scss`". Exempt `docs/design/tokens.md` and the archive.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` B7](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P2.

title: D7: turn `docs/README.md` into an intent router
body:
## Problem

It opens with a feature tour — quick start, project structure, tech stack. An agent (or a new contributor) arrives with an intent, not a curiosity about the stack.

## Proposed change

Lead with an *"I want to…"* table mapping intent → document, plus the four-kinds-of-memory table (specs · study · diary · traps). Keep the tour below the fold.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` D7](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P2.

title: D5: give use cases `UC-NNN` IDs and an index
body:
## Problem

21 use-case files named by slug, no IDs, no README, and three linking into a deleted archive. They cannot be cited from a spec, an issue, or a PR without pasting a path.

## Proposed change

Rename to `UC-NNN-slug.md`, add a `README.md` index table, and add the `specs:` frontmatter that the traceability gate checks.

Renaming 21 files is a `git mv` batch — do it with the audit-first discipline from `.cursor/rules/bulk-operation-safety.mdc`, and update the 18 inbound references in the same commit.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` D5](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P2.

title: E5: add a five-line `CLAUDE.md` pointer and record the single-instruction-file rule
body:
## Problem

There is no `CLAUDE.md`; Claude Code falls back to `AGENTS.md`, which works today but leaves the convention undocumented — so the next person who wants a Claude-specific rule will start a second instruction file.

## Proposed change

Five lines pointing at `AGENTS.md`, plus a "do not add project rules here" sentence. Record the rule as an ADR: *`AGENTS.md` is the single instruction file* — the value is in writing down **why** there is only one.

**Depends on** the ADR folder issue.

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` E5](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P2.

title: F3: add the sibling-repository rule to the pitfalls
body:
## Problem

Before inventing a convention — a doc format, a folder layout, an ID scheme — grep the sibling repository for it. Generalising from the one repo you happen to be looking at produces a parallel, weaker system whose vocabulary collides with the working one. Grundriss learned this the hard way and recorded it (an invented study system, replaced by the one that already existed).

## Proposed change

One paragraph in `docs/agent-workflows/agent-communication.md`, next to "do not guess table names from prompts" — same failure, larger scale.

## Live instance

`docs/study/STUDY-FORMAT.md` (landing with `cursor/upload-heic-hash-order-3be6`) was written from a secondhand record of Grundriss's format because that repo is not reachable from the agent environment. It carries a provenance note saying so and asking for reconciliation. **That note should not be deleted until the reconciliation actually happens.**

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` F3](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P2.

title: C1: make the component registry machine-readable and gated
body:
## Problem

The component registry is **1,370 lines of hand-maintained prose** across three supplements (75 `###` entries) versus **82** `*.component.ts` files in `shared/` alone plus the feature-local set. `scripts/validate-design-system-registry.mjs` validates a *different* registry (`docs/design/design-system/registry.json`, a schema check). Nothing compares the component catalog to the code — so the reuse gate, a Hard Blocker in `AGENTS.md`, rests on a document that can silently go stale.

## Proposed change

`docs/specs/component/registry.json` becomes the source (name, selector, path, spec, specId, useFor, notFor, slice). A generator renders the three supplements from it. A checker asserts:

1. every shared component has an entry
2. every entry's path and spec file exist
3. the entry's `specId` matches the spec's declared id
4. the rendered supplements are not stale

`docs/design/design-system/registry-format-decision.md` already chose JSON-as-source for the design-system registry; this extends the same decision one folder over.

**Largest single item in the adoption audit — schedule it as its own slice.**

**Source:** [`2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md` C1](https://github.com/matkleve/feldpost/blob/main/docs/audits/2026-09-08-grundriss-adoption.md) — P3, high impact.
